desc:
A workshop has two separate budgets of materials: budgetA units of material A and budgetB units of material B. There are n items, and item i consumes costA[i] units of A and costB[i] units of B. Each item can be made at most once.

Return the largest number of different items that can be made without exceeding either budget.
hints: This is a 0/1 knapsack, but with two capacity limits instead of one. The value of every item is simply 1.
Let best[a][b] be the largest number of items you can make using at most a units of A and at most b units of B, considering the items seen so far.
For each item, update the table in decreasing order of both a and b: best[a][b] = max(best[a][b], best[a-costA][b-costB] + 1). Iterating downwards stops the item being used twice.
editorial: Add the items one at a time. After processing some items, best[a][b] holds the maximum count achievable within budgets (a, b). When a new item with costs (x, y) arrives, either skip it (value unchanged) or make it, which is possible when a ≥ x and b ≥ y and yields best[a-x][b-y] + 1.

Updating in place requires visiting a from budgetA down to x and, inside it, b from budgetB down to y; this guarantees that the cell we read still reflects the state before the current item, so no item is counted twice. The running time is O(n · budgetA · budgetB) and the memory O(budgetA · budgetB).
